root_cause.text: Integer overflow in the xdr_round_up() operation when ticket_len is large causes the length check to be bypassed, potentially allowing an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the check from `xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - sizeof(container)` to `ticket_len > xdr_round_down(token_len - sizeof(container))`. The CVE description explicitly states "Rather than rounding up the value to be tested (which might overflow), round down the size of the available data." This confirms the overflow in the rounding-up step is the root cause.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the packet length validation in rxrpc token extraction to compare the ticket length against the rounded-down remaining buffer space instead of rounding up the ticket length, preventing potential buffer over-read.
intent_record.what: Changed the conditional check in rxgk_extract_token from comparing xdr_round_up(ticket_len) > token_len - sizeof(container) to comparing ticket_len > xdr_round_down(token_len - sizeof(container)).
intent_record.how: The original check rounded up the ticket length before comparing to the raw remaining length; the new check compares the raw ticket length to the rounded-down remaining length, ensuring that the token fits within aligned buffer boundaries and preventing potential out-of-bounds reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add xdr_round_down macro for symmetry with xdr_round_up to support future use cases.
intent_record.what: Added a new macro `xdr_round_down(x)` which calls `round_down((x), sizeof(__be32))`, alongside the existing `xdr_round_up(x)` macro.
intent_record.how: No immediate runtime behavior change; the macro is defined but not yet used. It provides a convenience for rounding values down to the nearest multiple of `sizeof(__be32)`.
